units.grammar_note: Every Spanish noun has a gender. Masculine nouns take el, feminine nouns take la. Most nouns ending in -o are masculine and most ending in -a are feminine, so the article changes while the noun stays put: el niño, la niña.

units.grammar_note: Adjectives come after the noun in Spanish and agree with it. A masculine noun takes -o, a feminine one takes -a, and plurals add -s: el tren rojo, la camisa roja, los zapatos azules.
